claims.text: Atomistic molecular dynamics can be used to investigate the thermal response of FeCuCrCoNi high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Specifically tailored multi-element interatomic potentials can capture the relevant interactions in FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles.
Molecular dynamics with tailored potentials can capture nanoparticle-size-dependent thermal behavior.
Smaller FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles exhibit enhanced surface diffusion relative to larger particles.
Smaller FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles undergo structural transitions earlier than larger particles.
The as-synthesized FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles are in a solid-solution state.
Finite-temperature atomistic simulations can reveal diffusion, chemical evolution, phase separation, and melting-related structural evolution in high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Smaller nanoparticles have a higher surface-to-volume ratio.
The higher surface-to-volume ratio of smaller FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles causes increased atomic diffusion, surface segregation, and phase separation.
A high surface-area-to-volume ratio intensifies thermal fluctuations and atomic mobility in smaller FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles.
Enhanced atomic mobility lowers the effective thermal stability of smaller FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles.
Larger FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles behave more like bulk material than smaller nanoparticles.
Significant diffusion and structural transitions begin at lower temperatures in smaller FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles than in larger ones.
At extremely small nanoparticle sizes, quantum effects or extreme surface reconstruction may dominate the thermal response.
At sufficiently large nanoparticle sizes, bulk-like properties may cause the predicted size dependence to diminish.
The accuracy of the molecular-dynamics predictions depends on the fidelity of the interatomic potential.
The exact transition-temperature thresholds and kinetic rates remain uncertain pending experimental validation and simulation refinement.
In situ electron-microscopy heating can be combined with molecular dynamics to evaluate nanoparticle thermal evolution.
